transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, thanks for having me. I guess what brings me in is... I just have this constant feeling like I've got a motor humming under my skin. It happens whenever I'm supposed to just sit still. 

Like, if I have to sit through a staff meeting at work, or even those event briefings at church, I just can't do it. I end up shifting around in my chair a lot, or standing up, or I just have to find some excuse to move around. It's getting pretty frustrating.
When did you first start noticing this feeling of needing to move around? Was it something that happened when you were a child, or is this more recent?

It's definitely not recent. It goes back to... well, to when I was a kid. I remember getting in trouble back in grade school for it. I was always popping out of my seat, or talking over the teacher. I'd just rush ahead and start doing things before the directions were even finished. My mother, she used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even back then. So yeah, it's been happening pretty much my whole life.

Besides the difficulty sitting still, do you also have trouble focusing or concentrating on tasks? For example, do you find it hard to keep your attention on one thing, or do you get easily distracted?

No, not really. I don't think I have much trouble with that. Like, when I'm working—I clean buildings for a living—I can pay attention to what I'm doing just fine. I don't really get sidetracked or lose focus on the job. 

It's more just... well, the physical part. As long as I'm moving around and doing the work, my mind stays on track. So, no, I wouldn't say I get easily distracted or have a hard time concentrating. It's just the sitting still that gets me.

You mentioned rushing ahead and starting things before directions were finished when you were younger. Do you still find yourself doing things impulsively or without thinking them through first, even now as an adult?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot when people are talking to me. Like, if my supervisor at work or one of the staff at church starts giving me instructions, I just... I jump in with what I think they're going to say before they even finish their sentence. 

I don't mean to be rude, I just kind of blurt it out. And the problem is, sometimes I guess wrong about what they were going to say, and then they have to stop and correct me. It happens pretty often.

You mentioned you can focus well on your cleaning job. But in other situations—like reading something important, following a conversation, or working on a task that requires you to sit and concentrate—do you find your mind wandering or do you lose track of what you're supposed to be doing?

No, not really. I mean, if I'm reading something, I just read it. I don't find my mind wandering off. And following a conversation... well, like I said, my problem is more that I interrupt people because I think I know what they're going to say, not because I'm spacing out or losing track of what we're talking about. I can concentrate fine, even if I have to sit down for a bit. It's just that sitting still makes me feel restless, not distracted.

When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting—like a hobby or something you like to do in your free time—do you still feel that restless need to move around, or can you settle into it more easily?

Well, even with stuff I like, it's still hard to just settle down. Like when I go fishing with my wife or we go to play bingo, things that are supposed to be relaxing... I still catch myself doing it. I'll be tapping my foot, or I'm talking too loud, or I'm constantly messing with my tackle box or my bingo dauber. It just gets hard for me to sit quietly and actually enjoy the activity without having to do something with my hands or keep moving.

Has this restlessness and need to move around caused you problems at work, or affected your relationships with people? For example, have you lost a job because of it, or has it caused conflict with your wife or others?

Well, I haven't lost my job, but... yeah, it is definitely causing some real issues at work. I've been getting complaints lately, and my supervisor has had to correct me a lot. 

Because I jump in and miss parts of the instructions, it ends up creating friction with the rest of the crew. It usually happens when we're trying to do room turnovers or when we're making decisions about our cleaning supplies. It actually got to the point recently where my supervisor sat me down and pushed me toward the employee assistance program. So... yeah, it's definitely making things difficult there.

When you have to do something that's not as interesting to you—like paying bills, filling out paperwork, or planning something—do you find it harder to stick with it or organize your thoughts compared to when you're doing your cleaning work?

Not really. I mean, paying bills or doing paperwork... nobody really likes doing that, but I don't have a hard time organizing my thoughts or sticking with it. I can get it done just fine. 

Like I was saying earlier, my mind doesn't wander off. It's really just the physical part of it. I'll be tapping my pen on the desk or shifting around in my chair a lot because I just want to get up and move. But the actual thinking part and getting the task finished? No, I don't have any trouble with that.

When you're in situations where you need to pay close attention to something for a while—like watching an important video at work, reading instructions carefully, or listening to someone explain something complex—do you ever find yourself having to re-read or re-listen to things because your mind wasn't fully on it, even if you weren't physically fidgeting?

No, not really. Like I said, my mind doesn't really wander. If I'm watching a training video or listening to somebody explain something, I hear what they're saying. I don't zone out or have to go back and figure out what I missed. It's just that while I'm listening, I might be bouncing my leg or wanting to get up. But my attention is there. I don't have a problem focusing my mind on it.

When you're supposed to organize multiple tasks or keep track of several things at once—like managing your cleaning supplies, scheduling appointments, or keeping your work area organized—do you find yourself forgetting steps, misplacing things, or having to go back and redo things because you skipped something?

No, I don't really have that problem. I keep track of my cleaning supplies just fine, and I always know where everything is on my cart. I don't really misplace things or forget my appointments, either. 

If I ever mess up a step, it's usually just because I jumped the gun and rushed into it, not because I forgot or lost track of what I was doing. So, no, keeping things organized or remembering what to do isn't really an issue for me. I'm pretty on top of all that.
